title: Event Registration Analytics Dashboard
distilled_summary: A reusable read-only Helix Lava Application pattern for one registration instance that separates people from registration records, keeps confirmed and wait-list populations explicit, compares weekly pace at the same event stage, supports optional campus and source attributes, models staff and serving segments with declared precedence, summarizes fee-item choices and demographics, and provides a bounded staff-only participant drilldown.

recipe.title: Event Registration Analytics Dashboard
recipe.summary: Build a secured read-only Helix dashboard for registration capacity, pace, wait list, optional segmentation, fee choices, demographics, and bounded participant drilldown.
use_cases: Give event teams one secured view of capacity, pace, wait list, choices, demographics, and participant context.
Compare a current registration instance with a prior event at the same number of days before registration closes.
Add optional mutually exclusive staff and serving segments without presenting local group semantics as universal Rock behavior.
outcomes: Registered people and registration records are reported as separate grains.
Confirmed, wait-list, weekly, segment, campus, demographic, fee-choice, and optional department metrics remain explicit and reconcilable.
Authorized staff can filter a bounded participant drilldown without exposing contact details or free-text registration answers.
prerequisites: A Rock registration instance with representative confirmed, wait-list, fee, and attribute data for validation.
Permission to create and secure a Helix Lava Application GET endpoint and page content block.
A reviewed definition for every optional campus, source, staff, serving-verifier, and department input.
A production-sized test plan for query cost, row cap, browser performance, and authorization.

adaptation_points.description: Set the locally verified registration instance. The public configuration uses zero and the endpoint stops until this is supplied.
adaptation_points.example: Use a local numeric ID; the recipe provides no working default.

adaptation_points.description: Optionally set a comparable prior instance whose end date can anchor same-stage pace comparison.
adaptation_points.example: Leave zero to disable prior-event metrics.

adaptation_points.description: Set a fallback only when RegistrationInstance.MaxAttendees is intentionally empty.
adaptation_points.example: Leave zero when no fallback is appropriate.

adaptation_points.description: Map optional registrant campus and discovery-source Attribute IDs after confirming entity scope and display semantics.
adaptation_points.example: registrantCampusAttributeId and sourceAttributeId remain zero by default.

adaptation_points.description: Configure optional staff and serving-verifier groups, then confirm active non-archived membership is the intended truth source.
adaptation_points.example: staffGroupId and servingVerifierGroupId remain zero by default.

adaptation_points.description: Configure a serving root group and department group type only when the local hierarchy supports that interpretation.
adaptation_points.example: servingRootGroupId and departmentGroupTypeId remain zero by default.

adaptation_points.description: Confirm fee items represent participant choices and optionally restrict displayed fee groups by name.
adaptation_points.example: Leave feeGroupNameContains empty to include every qualifying fee group.

adaptation_points.description: Optionally remove a display-only suffix such as a target-audience annotation without modifying fee-item source names.
adaptation_points.example: Set an empty string to disable label cleanup.

adaptation_points.description: Choose a bounded local drilldown cap between 1 and 1000 after measuring database and browser cost.
Restrict both the Rock page and Lava Application View action to authenticated roles approved for participant operations.

security.authorization: Application-view and page permissions limited to approved registration operations roles
notes: Read-only participant names, attendance intent, staff/serving classification, and registration choices remain sensitive operational data.
The public reference omits email, phone, addresses, payment details, arbitrary attributes, and free-text registration answers.
The endpoint enables only Sql and uses GET only while it performs no writes.
A future write action requires a separate endpoint with authorization, CSRF protection, validation, audit logging, and rollback planning.
The production pattern was reviewed against the Rock 17/18 model family, but the sanitized package has not been deployed unchanged in every supported release.
Verify RegistrationInstance, RegistrationRegistrant, RegistrationRegistrantFee, AttributeValue, GroupMember, and Lava SQL behavior against the target release.
The reference uses SQL Server window functions and STRING_AGG; performance depends on data volume, indexes, compatibility level, and optional hierarchy depth.

files.purpose: Adaptation, metrics, security, performance, validation, compatibility, and rollback guidance
License for the public recipe package
Public-safe application rigging with disabled optional modules and no working production IDs
Read-only aggregate queries, responsive dashboard, and bounded participant drilldown
Executable public-boundary, configuration, metric, row-cap, and no-mutation checks

instructions: Review the immutable README, configuration, Lava source, and static contract before adaptation.
Create a secured GET endpoint with ApplicationView security and enable only the Sql Lava command.
Set registrationInstanceId, then add optional prior-instance, attribute, segment, hierarchy, and fee configuration only after documenting their local meaning.
Render the endpoint through a Lava Application Content block on a staff-authorized page.
Run the static contract and test query plans with representative production volume.
Validate metric invariants, wait-list behavior, multi-person registrations, optional adapters, authorization personas, and desktop/mobile rendering before launch.
validation_steps: Run python3 tests/static_contract.py from the recipe directory.
Confirm registered people match a known instance total and registrations differ correctly for a multi-person registration.
Confirm wait-list people are excluded from confirmed aggregates and remain explicit in the separate metric and drilldown.
Confirm mutually exclusive segment counts sum exactly to confirmed people and staff precedence handles a person who also satisfies serving verification.
Confirm campus and source values use the intended registrant attributes rather than person or registration campus by accident.
Confirm fee-choice counts against known selections and review active versus historical fee behavior.
Confirm a serving-verifier holder without an active department lands in the verifier-only bucket and multi-department totals disclose possible duplication.
Confirm prior-stage comparison is absent when disabled and aligns by days remaining when configured.
Confirm the row cap, empty state, reset, search, campus, segment, and detail controls behave correctly.
Confirm unauthorized users cannot open the page or endpoint and an administrator override is not mistaken for intended-role access.
Confirm rendered output has no Lava or browser-console errors, clipped labels, or internal vertical scrolling at desktop and mobile widths.
rollback_steps: Disable or remove the Lava Application endpoint and page block.
Restore the previous page and application configuration; no data rollback is required because the recipe performs no writes.
known_limitations: The sanitized package requires live testing in each target Rock release and instance configuration.
Client-side drilldown filtering is intentionally capped and should become server-side pagination for large events.
BirthYear-derived age bands are approximate and are not exact birthday calculations.
Fee items are not universally breakout choices; the target registration template determines their meaning.
Group-based staff, serving, and department classifications are optional local semantics rather than built-in universal Rock definitions.
Department totals can exceed unique serving people because group membership is many-to-many.
learnings: Declare metric grain because one Registration can contain multiple RegistrationRegistrant rows.
Define confirmed and wait-list predicates once, then reconcile every segment and distribution against that population.
Compare registration pace by days remaining until close rather than calendar date.
Use explicit classification precedence so staff and serving segments remain mutually exclusive.
Treat verifier groups and department hierarchies as configurable local truth sources, not as universal Rock behavior.
Distinguish registrant attribute campus from registration campus and person campus before labeling a chart.
Interpret fee items as choices only after reviewing the registration template and active or historical behavior.
Clean display labels without mutating source registration option names.
A read-only endpoint still requires application and page authorization because participant operations data is sensitive.
Bound the drilldown and measure query plans before increasing row limits.
Verify rendered metrics, authorization, errors, and responsive overflow after content readback; a successful file write alone is not proof of a working dashboard.

title: Reconcile event registration dashboard metrics by grain and population
distilled_summary: Before trusting an event-registration dashboard, name each metric grain and population explicitly. Count RegistrationRegistrant rows for people and distinct Registration rows for registration records; do not label them interchangeably. Define confirmed and wait-list predicates once, apply them to every chart, and test invariants such as confirmed people equaling the sum of mutually exclusive segments and each one-value distribution. Test a multi-person registration, a wait-list registrant, and a recent registrant. For historical pace, align events by days remaining until registration closes rather than calendar date. Do not require many-to-many department totals to equal unique people; disclose that exception and validate it separately.

title: Treat staff and serving segments as configured local truth with explicit precedence
distilled_summary: When a registration report segments people by staff, serving, or department, document the local truth source instead of presenting the categories as built-in universal Rock semantics. Use only active, non-archived memberships in reviewed groups, apply an explicit mutually exclusive precedence such as staff before serving, and reconcile the segment total to confirmed registrants. Gate department reporting behind a reviewed serving verifier when that is the operating definition, preserve a verifier-only or unassigned bucket, and disclose that one person may count in multiple departments. Leave the module disabled when the target instance cannot define and validate the groups or hierarchy.

title: Validate rendered Helix dashboards after exact content readback
distilled_summary: After an exact Rock file-content readback confirms the intended Helix or Lava Application source was saved, validate the rendered dashboard as a separate gate. Test an unauthorized visitor, the intended staff role, and an administrator without treating admin override as proof of role access. Assert known metric invariants and representative rows, inspect visible and hidden Lava error surfaces plus browser-console errors, exercise filters and empty states, and measure responsive layout for clipped labels, unintended internal vertical scrolling, and bounded horizontal overflow. Content equality proves deployment targeting; rendered checks prove authorization, data semantics, JavaScript behavior, and layout in the actual page context.
